column1: Methods & Research Techniques Used in This Model
Short reference for the team and for the interim presentation.

column2: One Inputs sheet, three scenario columns and a switch. Every output is a formula, so new evidence updates everything.
Guests × spend per daypart (morning/lunch/afternoon/dinner) + delivery + events + retail. More defensible than a single 'covers per day' number.
Demand is tested against seats × hours ÷ dwell time. RevPASH = revenue per available seat-hour; benchmark it against observed venues.
Linear ramp from month-1 % to 100% at maturity; Ramadan/Lebaran & December indices. Parsa (S36): early months are where most restaurants fail – fund them.
Items classed by contribution margin vs popularity to set prices and the blended food-cost %.
Fixed costs ÷ contribution-margin % → revenue/day and guests/day. Margin of safety = how far revenue can fall before losses.
Unlevered project cash flows incl. rent prepayment timing; payback month from the cumulative line; 5-year IRR with optional terminal value.
District rents from asking-price evidence (P25/median/P75), service charges, weighted scoring, and occupancy-cost % vs revenue. Upgrade: Huff gravity model (S40, S41).
Each driver ±flex while others stay at base; sorted by EBITDA swing. Two-way grids show interactions (volume × price, volume × rent).
1,000 triangular draws per driver between conservative and optimistic values → probability of loss and of payback within 3/5 years.
For each key input: desk source + listing/quote + interview. Disagreement between sources becomes the scenario range.
Footfall counts (15-min samples × dayparts), seat-occupancy and dwell timing at comparables, menu-price scraping (dine-in & GoFood), broker & operator interviews (5–8), supplier quotes.
Asking rents ≠ deal rents; menu and food costs are illustrative; tax simplified; no VAT/PBJT cash timing; independent Monte Carlo draws; legal structure unverified.
